summary: As of mid-to-late 2026, ChatGPT/GPT-5 retains the largest share of consumer web traffic at 55.5% but faces rapid erosion from Gemini (25.6%) and Claude (9.3%), while in enterprise API usage Anthropic leads at 40% followed by OpenAI at 27% and Google at 21%. The open-source segment is intensely competitive, with DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Meta Llama 4, Qwen3, and emerging models like Kimi K2.6 and MiniMax M3 challenging proprietary incumbents on benchmarks at a fraction of the cost. Developer adoption is increasingly fragmented across providers, with OpenRouter data showing DeepSeek leading API text request share at 24.4%, signaling a meaningful shift away from OpenAI's historic API dominance.

models.name: GPT-5 / GPT-5.1
models.popularity_notes: ChatGPT holds 55.5% of worldwide generative AI web visits as of August 2026 (Similarweb), and OpenAI leads enterprise API deployments at 27% share (Menlo Ventures 2025), making it the single most-used LLM platform globally despite year-over-year share decline.
strengths: Broadest ecosystem and plugin integrations
Strong multi-step reasoning and tool use
Massive developer familiarity and documentation
General-purpose performance across nearly all task types
Real-time capabilities via ChatGPT integration
models.best_for: General-purpose enterprise and consumer applications requiring reliable, well-supported API access

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.popularity_notes: Google Gemini's web visits surged from 527.7 million in May 2025 to 2.9 billion in May 2026 (roughly 450% growth per Similarweb), capturing 25.6% of generative AI web traffic by August 2026 and 21% of enterprise API usage.
strengths: Longest context window among top proprietary models
Deep integration with Google Workspace and Search
Strong multimodal capabilities (text, image, audio, video)
Fastest-growing consumer adoption of any model in 2026
Competitive benchmark performance on reasoning tasks
models.best_for: Multimodal workflows, long-document analysis, and organizations embedded in the Google ecosystem

models.name: Claude Opus 5 / Claude Fable 5.1
models.popularity_notes: Claude holds 9.3% of generative AI web visits (Similarweb, August 2026), leads enterprise API spend at 40% share (Menlo Ventures), and Claude Fable 5.1 tops the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 66 as of September 2026.
strengths: Highest enterprise API adoption by spend at 40%
Top-ranked on Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index
Industry-leading safety and alignment properties
Exceptional long-document comprehension and summarization
855% year-over-year web traffic growth (Similarweb)
models.best_for: Enterprise applications requiring safety-critical outputs, complex reasoning, and long-context document processing

models.name: DeepSeek-V4-Pro
models.popularity_notes: DeepSeek leads OpenRouter API text request share at 24.4% as of the week of September 21, 2026, and DeepSeek-V4-Pro tops the Onyx Open LLM Leaderboard in SWE-bench, LiveCodeBench, and bug-fixing benchmarks.
strengths: Leads API marketplace usage on OpenRouter at 24.4% of text requests
Top open-source model for coding and bug-fixing (SWE-bench, LiveCodeBench)
Developed with significantly less compute than comparable proprietary models
Strong reasoning capabilities as successor to the viral DeepSeek R1
Highly cost-efficient relative to performance tier
models.best_for: Cost-sensitive developers needing frontier-class coding and reasoning via open-weight self-hosting or API

models.name: Llama 4
models.popularity_notes: Meta Llama 4 is ranked among the top five AI LLMs of 2026 by multiple analyst sources and is the leading open-weight model for general reasoning, with massive HuggingFace download volume driven by Meta's open-release strategy.
models.cost_input: Free (self-hosted); ~$0.10–$0.30 per 1M tokens via hosted APIs
models.cost_output: Free (self-hosted); ~$0.30–$0.90 per 1M tokens via hosted APIs
strengths: Most widely downloaded open-weight model family on HuggingFace
Permissive licensing enabling commercial self-hosting
Strong general reasoning and instruction-following
Broad community ecosystem and fine-tune library
Recommended by analysts as top open alternative to GPT-5
models.best_for: Teams requiring self-hosted or on-premise deployment with no per-token API costs

models.name: Qwen3 / Qwen3-235B-A22B
models.popularity_notes: The Qwen family has been adopted by over 90,000 enterprises globally (Shakudo, 2026), and Qwen3-235B-A22B-Thinking has redefined the open-weights landscape with over 1 trillion parameters and support for 119 languages.
strengths: Adopted by over 90,000 enterprises worldwide
Broadest multilingual support at 119 languages
Parameter scale exceeding 1 trillion in largest variant
Strong on code generation benchmarks (Qwen3.6-27B)
Active open-source community with frequent releases
models.best_for: Multilingual enterprise deployments, Asian-language tasks, and large-scale self-hosted reasoning workloads

models.name: Grok-3 / Grok-4
models.popularity_notes: Grok holds 2.4% of generative AI web visits (Similarweb, August 2026) and is ranked among the top five LLMs of 2026 by multiple sources, with Grok-4 offering a 2 million token context window and among the lowest API prices at its tier.
strengths: Largest context window of any listed model at 2M tokens
Real-time information access via X platform integration
Extremely competitive API pricing at $0.20 per 1M input tokens
Strong performance on reasoning benchmarks
Witty conversational experience suited to consumer use
models.best_for: Real-time information retrieval tasks, ultra-long context workloads, and cost-optimized API deployments

models.name: Mistral Large
models.popularity_notes: Mistral Large is consistently ranked by analysts as a top open-source model for speed and efficiency in 2026, maintains strong HuggingFace download counts, and is a preferred choice among European enterprises for GDPR-compliant self-hosting.
strengths: Best-in-class inference speed among large open-weight models
Strong multilingual performance, especially European languages
Permissive licensing suitable for commercial self-hosting
Efficient mixture-of-experts architecture
Preferred for GDPR-compliant EU deployments
models.best_for: Latency-sensitive production APIs and European organizations requiring data-sovereign self-hosted deployment

models.name: GLM-5.2
models.popularity_notes: GLM-5.2 achieves the highest GPQA Diamond score among all open-source models on the Onyx Open LLM Leaderboard (updated July 2026) and is ranked as the top open-source model for reasoning, signaling rapid rising developer adoption in 2026.
strengths: Highest GPQA Diamond score among open-source models (Onyx Leaderboard)
Top-ranked open-source model for complex reasoning tasks
Strong bilingual (Chinese/English) capabilities
Competitive with frontier proprietary models on science benchmarks
Rapidly rising adoption among research and developer communities
models.best_for: Research applications and reasoning-intensive workloads requiring open-weight access with near-frontier benchmark performance

models.name: Kimi K2.6 / Kimi K3
models.popularity_notes: Kimi K2.6 appears on the Onyx Open LLM Leaderboard in July 2026 across four separate benchmark categories — bug fixing, code generation, reasoning, and general performance — indicating broad developer adoption and cross-domain strength among emerging open models.
strengths: Top-ranked across four benchmark categories on Onyx Leaderboard (July 2026)
Strong code generation rivaling DeepSeek-V4-Pro
Excellent reasoning scores alongside GLM-5.2
Rapid iteration cycle with multiple major releases in 2026
Emerging open-source alternative with frontier-class performance
models.best_for: Developers seeking a rapidly improving open-weight model competitive across coding, reasoning, and general tasks
